metadata.case_name: CHAN SAI CHIU v. CHING YAN CHEUK T/A EDEN CONNECTIONS DESIGN & ENGINEERING CO

plaintiff.occupation_before: casual general labourer in decoration industry

injuries.description: deep laceration of left index finger pulp
source: Dr Lams diagnosis of the injury was deep laceration of left index finger pulp.
an irregular dirty wound associated with tissue and skin loss was noted over the pulp of his left index finger.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of finger or thumb

manifestations.description: persistent numbness and pain over his left index finger
atrophy of the left index finger pulp
slight decrease in range of motion of the left index finger joints
mild decrease in grip strength and significant decrease in pinch grip with left index finger
hypersensitive and stiffness at his left index finger
unable to resume work after the sick leave (initially)

treatments_received: A&E treatment at the Ruttonjee & Tang Shiu Kin Hospitals (TSKH)
wound dressing at the Shek Kip Mei General Out Patient Clinic
treatments_future: occupational therapy with desensitization program (six weeks, three sessions per week)

losses.description: General damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenities resulting from deep laceration of left index finger pulp

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Yun San v Cheung Yue Yiu trading as Radio Engineering Co
comparable_cases.injury_description: claimants left index and middle fingers were injured in the accident by a circular saw. He was found to have sustained a crush injury to his left middle and index fingers. There was pulp loss in his left index finger and a deep laceration in the middle finger exposing extensor tendon over proximal interphalangeal joint. X-ray showed communited intra-articular fracture of the condyle of the proximal phalanx of the left middle finger. He had undergone two surgical operations.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Hung Hang v Fat Kee Marine Repairing & Engineering Co Limited and Anor
comparable_cases.injury_description: claimant welder injured his right middle finger in the accident. He was found to have suffered crush injury to his right middle finger. Physical examination revealed bruise and tenderness over the tip of the right middle finger and subungal haematoma over nail. The active range of motion was decreased although flexion and extension mechanism was intact. X-ray showed fracture of the tuft of distal phalanx of the right middle finger.
